The Bobcats were led by fourth-year head coach [[Jeff Boals]], who was a 1995 graduate of Ohio University.{{cite web|url=https://ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbball/roster/coaches/jeff-boals/132|title=Jeff Boals|website=Ohio University Athletics|language=en|access-date=May 15, 2022}}{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/coaches/jeff-boals-1.html|title=Jeff Boals|website=Sports Reference|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}} They played their home games at the [[Convocation Center (Ohio University)|Convocation Center]] in [[Athens, Ohio]] as a member of the [[Mid-American Conference]].{{cite web |url=https://www.ohio.edu/building-directory/convocation-center|title=Convocation Center|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}{{cite web |url=https://getsomemaction.com/standings.aspx?standings=182|title=2022-23 Men's Basketball Standings|website=Mid-American Conference|language=en|access-date=2022-11-11}} Ohio started the season slow after key player losses from the prior year. They also started [[2022–23 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|conference play]] slowly with several difficult road games in January. They recovered in February and won seven out of their last nine regular season games to head into the [[2023 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] at 18–13 as the fifth seed with a 10–8 [[2022–23 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|conference record]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/standings/_/season/2023/group/14|publisher=ESPN|title=MAC Basketball Standings - 2022-23|access-date=March 3, 2022}} They defeated [[2022–23 Ball State Cardinals men's basketball team|Ball State]] in the first round of the [[2023 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] before losing to top-seeded [[2022–23 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]] to finish 19–14.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401514305|title=Ohio 90, Ball State 70|publisher=ESPN|access-date=March 9, 2023}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401514308|title=Ohio 75, Toledo 82|publisher=ESPN|access-date=March 10, 2023}} ==Previous season== {{main|2021–22 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team}} The [[2021–22 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Bobcats]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 25–10 and 14–6 in [[2021–22 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|MAC play]] to finish in third place.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/standings/_/group/14 |title=MAC Basketball Standings - 2021-22 |website=ESPN|access-date=September 6, 2022}} As the No. 3 seed in the [[2022 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 Ball State Cardinals men's basketball team|Ball State]] before losing to [[2021–22 Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball team|Kent State]] in the semi-finals.{{cite web|url=https://getsomemaction.com/tournaments/?id=162&path=mbball|accessdate=February 1, 2022|title=2022 MAC Men's Basketball Championship|publisher=Mid-American Conference}} They received a bid to the [[2022 College Basketball Invitational|CBI]].{{cite web |title=Schedule |url=https://www.gazellegroup.com/main/cbi/schedule-2/ |website=College Basketball Invitational |publisher=Gazelle Group |date=March 2022 |access-date=March 20, 2022}} There they defeated [[2021–22 Rice Owls men's basketball team|Rice]] in the first round before losing to [[2021–22 Abilene Christian Wildcats men's basketball team|Abilene Christian]] in the second round.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401411723|title=Sears lifts Ohio past Rice on late shot|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-09-30}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401411731|title=Ohio 86, Abilene Christian 91|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-09-30}} ==Offseason== Ohio had a lot of roster turnover. Eleven of the sixteen players that had minutes the prior season either graduated, left the team, or transferred. Three key starters had to be replaced. Jason Carter graduated while [[Ben Vander Plas]] and [[Mark Sears]] transferred to high-major programs.
